gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Samsung B-series soundbar's own lip-sync control only delays audio (0–300 ms) and is 'Not available in "USB" or "BT" mode'. Over Bluetooth, the audio is already the late signal, so this setting cannot fix Bluetooth lag. The fix has to be HDMI ARC or optical, or a setting on the TV.
standout_why: I opened the cited itechguides.com how-to guide and geekchamp.com's '5 Soundbars' page. Both tell shoppers to fix Bluetooth lag by adjusting 'Audio Delay, AV Sync, or Lip Sync'. geekchamp gives PCWorld's figure of up to about 150 ms. Both say the TV must support Bluetooth audio output. Neither says that soundbar sync controls only add delay and are disabled in Bluetooth mode on the Samsung models ChatGPT showed. I could not read the body of the other cited page, whathifi.com, or rtings.com: both returned only navigation.
decides: This supports choosing a soundbar connected by HDMI ARC or optical (Sony HT-S100F, Samsung HW-B630F) over a Bluetooth-only TV link. A shopper who answers ChatGPT's follow-up with 'Bluetooth only' loses the soundbar's lip-sync correction. A portable speaker such as the Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen has no such control to begin with. If the shopper wants a cable-free setup, any lip-sync fix has to come from the TV's own settings.

findings.label: Soundbar lip-sync (AUDIO SYNC) range and Bluetooth restriction
findings.value: Audio delay 0–300 ms; 'Not available in "USB" or "BT" mode.'
findings.source_title: Samsung HW-B650 Manual, page 10 (ENG-10), also lists HW-B660
findings.note: Samsung's full-manual text, quoted: 'If the video on the TV and audio from the Soundbar are not synchronised… select AUDIO SYNC… set the audio delay between 0~300 milliseconds… (Not available in "USB" or "BT" mode.)' The control can only add delay to the audio. Bluetooth makes the audio late, so even if the control worked in BT mode, it would push the audio further behind. This is a sibling model, so I have not confirmed that the HW-B630F manual's sync section has the same wording.

findings.label: TV-over-Bluetooth support in the maker's manual
findings.value: 'When a TV is connected using Bluetooth, you can hear stereo sound without the hassle of cabling.' 'Only one TV can be connected at a time.'
findings.source_title: Samsung HW-B630F Mode d'emploi (English section), page 23 of 86
findings.note: Pairing steps: press PAIR to enter 'BT PAIRING', select Bluetooth mode on the TV, then choose '[AV] B-Series Soundbar'. This page says nothing about delay.

findings.label: Bluetooth connection priority for Samsung TVs
findings.value: 'Only 1 Samsung TV, or 2 Bluetooth devices can be connected to the Soundbar at one time.' 'The Soundbar will be disconnected from Bluetooth devices when it receives a connection request from a Samsung TV.'
findings.source_title: Samsung HW-B630F Mode d'emploi (English section), page 31
findings.note: A Samsung TV connecting over Bluetooth knocks a phone off the soundbar. This matters to shoppers who also want to stream music from a phone.

findings.label: Rival coverage of Bluetooth lag (baseline for the gap)
findings.value: Up to about 150 ms (PCWorld figure, reported by geekchamp); roughly 40–50 ms with aptX Low Latency/Adaptive only when both ends share the codec
findings.source_title: Best Bluetooth TV Speakers in 2026: 5 Soundbars for Better TV Audio (geekchamp)
findings.note: These are geekchamp's secondhand figures, not the makers' and not measured. I include them to show what the rival pages already cover.
